May I, in the future, never hear evil sounds nor see evil people. [I now turn toward the World-Honored One.]
Prostrating with the five limbs touching the ground, we seek mercy and repent: "We, the ignorant, have committed many evil deeds.
Lacking shame and remorse, we have violated the five precepts, the eight precepts, and the full precepts; we have stolen the property of the Saṃgha and the property of the present assembly;

we have preached the Dharma impurely; and we have adorned ourselves with various evil karmas, even committing the five heinous crimes and the ten evil acts, possessing all manner of unwholesome states."
I shall surely fall into the evil realms and suffer endless pain. [○@叩] I only pray that Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, with voices of great compassion,
will extensively expound for me the true reality (*dharmatā*) of all phenomena and the methods for extinguishing sinful karma, so that upon hearing them,
I may resolve to attain Bodhicitta and immediately behold the vast and expansive features of the World of Ultimate Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*), and see the bodies of the Buddhas.

The two bodhisattvas attained great awakening and reached the stage of non-arising patience (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*). At the time of their death, Amitābha Buddha extended his hand to welcome them;
never leaving the golden platform, they traveled throughout the worlds of the ten directions, receiving successive predictions of enlightenment (*vyākaraṇa*) before all the Buddhas.
Returning to his own country, he paid homage to the hundred-treasure lotus and extensively proclaimed the Buddha’s words for the sake of the great multitude.
His *saṃnāha* (armor) of great compassion shall endure until the end of the future. (Recite this three times. Then rise and say:)
Having completed the repentance and made the vows, take refuge and pay homage to the Triple Gem (bow). Next, rise, take up the incense, and hold the censer according to the *samādhi* ritual.

Practice the path with a sincere mind, visualizing descending onto the surface of the lotus-pool water. As you lift and set down your feet, lotuses emerge and submerge; visualize each detail—the shoulders and backs of the three figures, the folds of their celestial robes, and so forth—clearly and with perfect clarity. Recite as follows:
Namo Amitābha Buddha. Namo Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Namo Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva. (Recite seven times or more.

Next, recite the "Chapter on Miscellaneous Contemplations" seven times or more. Then again, as above, recite the three names. Visualize returning to their original positions upon the flowers. Perform the Three Refuges.)
Taking refuge in the Buddha, may all beings realize the Great Way and give rise to the unsurpassed mind.
Taking refuge in the Dharma, may all beings enter deeply into the treasury of the scriptures, their wisdom like the ocean.
Taking refuge in the Sangha, may all beings lead and harmonize the great assembly, free from all hindrances.

Having paid homage to the assembly of noble ones, one next practices seated meditation by contemplating the *ūrṇā-kośa* (white tuft) of a standing Buddha. The interior of the tuft is hollow; it measures two and a half inches in circumference.

It has eight facets and curls to the right, situated between the eyebrows. It is polished, pure, and translucent, shining brilliantly against the golden countenance. Its boundaries are clearly defined.
It is clearly manifest. Again, it arises; the brush-tip extends downward, its length falling one foot short of the flower pedestal.
It brilliantly reflects the golden body and the flower-feet, while the lapis lazuli water shines and touches one’s own person.

When this visualization has been firmly established through long practice, it is also excellent to perform a single cycle of prostration while seated upright, visualizing the aforementioned ritual. Question: For what reason is the rank of the Buddhas being prostrated to as it is?
[Question: It is cumbersome and redundant. [Answer: This is for the sake of refining the path of contemplation, so that whether the eyes are open or closed, [the object] appears clearly before one.

One should know that the practice of contemplation does not go beyond the two methods of the general and the specific. Initially, the general is not as effective as the specific, because the general is brief while the specific is detailed.

If one were to perform the rites separately over a long period, it would not be as effective as performing them collectively, because the separate rites are gradual while the collective rite is sudden and complete. Question:

Having already made the announcement to Śākyamuni upon entering the maṇḍala, why does one again announce to Amitābha at the time of repentance? Answer: It is because only through the persistent and earnest cultivation of both longing [for rebirth] and revulsion [toward saṃsāra] can one attain birth in the Pure Land.

Thus, one makes the announcement to the Original Teacher (Śākyamuni) through the mental faculty (*manas-karma*), and to the Guiding Teacher (Amitābha) through the vocal faculty (*vāk-karma*). This repetition in the text serves to express single-minded devotion; such is the nature of the act of announcing.
The Buddha to whom the petition is addressed is neither redundant nor erroneous. Question: For what reason is the ūrṇā-kośa (white tuft of hair) also observed? Answer:

Both the superior and inferior observations take the ūrṇā-kośa as their initial step. This is why the wise examine the characteristics of the inferior marks within the ūrṇā-kośa of the superior marks;
the intent of the commentary lies precisely in this chapter. Later generations, such as the Repentance Master Ciyun and others, all... [text ends].

This contemplation is supported because it perfectly accords with the essential meaning of the sutra. Furthermore, since those in the末法 (mofa) age have dull faculties and may find even inferior contemplations difficult to practice, the objective realm of this primary contemplation is detailed in the ritual procedures (*xingyi*).

This allows the practitioner to master the contemplation of the white tuft (*śvetabhrū*) naturally and without perceiving its difficulty, as the preceding textual meanings in the sutra are already established. Therefore, one should focus [on this].

This is intended for cultivation while seated. Furthermore, fearing that those who are not yet skilled in contemplating the white curl (*ūrṇā-kośa*) might falter, one is instructed to silently contemplate the ritual of prostration while seated.

Since the practice of contemplation becomes even more easily accomplished once one has performed the ritual of prostration, movement and stillness, as well as phenomena and principle, are pressed together and mutually investigated.

Through the skillful refinement of both general and specific aspects—where the white curl serves as the general [object] and the primary visualization as the specific—the mind is thoroughly permeated.

By means of this, one responds to the final age; perhaps this may be called "skillfully conforming to the capacities and conditions. The details regarding the single mind and the three contemplations are fully explained in the *Miaozong* (The Wondrous Pivot); they shall not be elaborated upon here.

The Ritual for Reciting and Practicing the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* (The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on Amitābha) Based on the Gate of Samādhi for Beginners in the *Contemplation of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life*.
Compiled by the later-generation śramaṇa Chengshi of Guśi, following the scriptures.
(The practitioner faces west while preparing the chamber. As they enter and exit, they recite the name of Amitābha Buddha.

Upon entering, they should contemplate as follows: “The Buddha told Śāriputra: ‘Those who hear this sutra and uphold it, as well as those who hear the names of the various Buddhas, shall all be protected and remembered by all the Buddhas. They shall all attain non-retrogression from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.’”

Therefore, Śāriputra, you all should believe and accept my words as well as those spoken by all the Buddhas. Having formed this visualization, one should then visualize the Original Teacher, the Guide, and all the Triple Gem of the ten directions, and chant with a sincere heart: ( )
With all reverence, with a single mind, I prostrate before the eternally abiding Triple Gem of the ten directions (contemplate as follows):
"The Three Jewels and their three virtues are like space; The three obstructions of sentient beings are likewise so.
Therefore, with impartiality, I universally take refuge and pay homage; May we swiftly enter together the ocean of the Dharma-realm."
(The presiding master rises and announces:
"All these members of the assembly shall each kneel in turn, solemnly holding incense and flowers, and make offerings according to the Dharma.

(The assembly scatters flowers while chanting together: "We make offerings to the Triple Gem throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm. (Holding the incense burner, one visualizes that this incense and these flowers pervade the ten directions, etc. Having completed the visualization, one speaks again:)

May these clouds of incense and flowers fill the worlds of the ten directions, making offerings to all Buddhas, to the Dharma difficult for the world to believe, and to all those who are supreme and virtuous; may they universally perfume all sentient beings, causing them all to resolve upon Bodhicitta.
(The phrases "Dharma Jewel" and "Sangha Jewel" are specific in wording but universal in meaning. Next, the invocation proceeds:)

Having made offerings, all pay homage with reverence (bowing). Use the aforementioned general visualization verse for the following sections: the eulogy, the confession, the three refuges, and the place of prostration; in each case, employ this verse. Next, arise and set up the incense burner, and offer praise as follows:
The radiance of his body is inconceivable, Shining universally throughout the ten directions.
Tathāgata Immeasurable Light, the Great Compassionate Father in the West, His lifespan is inconceivable, Boundless asaṃkhyeya—Tathāgata Amitāyus.
The Great Guide in the West, Whose land is purely and utterly pure.
Adorned with merit, may all sentient beings Together ascend the stage of non-retrogression.
The Buddhas of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, Unite in praising this land;
Therefore, I and all sentient beings vow to be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. (Prostrate. Having finished the visualization, rise and offer incense, saying:)
With single-minded devotion, prostrate to Śākyamuni Buddha, the Original Teacher in this Sahā world of the five turbidities and evil age.

(Visualize that because the karma of his own body and that of sentient beings is heavy, he entered this evil age as the Greatly Compassionate Original Teacher to preach the Dharma that is difficult to believe. One should feel extreme pity and gratitude for this benevolent virtue. Visualize and say:
"The nature of the one who prostrates and the one to whom one prostrates is empty and still; the resonance between cause and effect is inconceivable."
This my place of enlightenment is like a celestial jewel, within which the shadow of Śākyamuni Tathāgata appears;
my own body’s shadow appears before the Tathāgata, as I seek rebirth and prostrate at his feet.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Buddhas of the eastern world: Akṣobhya Buddha, Sumeru-lakṣaṇa Buddha, and Mahāsumeru Buddha.
To the Buddha Sumeruprabha, the Buddha Mañjughoṣa, and all such Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River—[the subsequent verses are all the same as above;

only the names are changed according to each position]. Visualize these Buddhas extending their broad and long tongues to cover the great trichiliocosm, speaking words of truth to exhort and inspire rebirth [in the Pure Land]. One should receive this with utmost faith and without any doubt or hesitation. [The following six prostrations are all the same.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Buddhas of the southern world: Buddhalocanapradīpa, Yaśaḥprabha, and Mahārciskandha.
To the Buddha Sumerudīpa, the Buddha Aparimitavīrya, and all such Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
I prostrate with one mind; and to the Buddha Amitāyus of the Western World, the Buddha Amitalaksana, the Buddha Amitadhvaja, the Buddha Mahāprabha,
the Buddha Mahāvairocana, the Buddha Ratnalakṣaṇa, and the Buddha Viśuddhaprabha, and all such Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
With one mind,
all Buddhas pay homage to the Buddhas of the northern world, such as the Buddha Flame-Shoulder, the Buddha Most Excellent Sound, the Buddha Unstoppable, the Buddha Sun-Born,
and the Buddha Net-Luminosity, as well as to all other Buddhas there, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Buddhas of the four intermediate directions: the Buddha King of the Most Supreme, Vast Cloud-Thunder Sound;
the Buddha of Supreme Sunlight, Renown, and Merit; the Buddha Radiance of the King of Fire with Immeasurable Merit;

and the Buddha of Countless Hundreds of Thousands of Koṭis of Vast Wisdom—namely, all such Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges (abbreviated according to the Tang translation and the *Sukhāvatī-vyūha-sūtra* Repentance Rite; supplemented in total).
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate before the Buddhas of the world-systems below: the Buddha Siṃha, the Buddha Yaśas, the Buddha Yaśaprabha, the Buddha Dharma,
the Buddha Dharmadhvaja, the Buddha Dharmadharin, and all such Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.

With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Buddhas of the world above: Brahmā-voice Buddha, Constellation King Buddha, Supreme Fragrance Buddha, Fragrant Light Buddha, Great Flame Shoulder Buddha,
Adorned with Various Colored Jewel Flower Bodies Buddha, Śāla Tree King Buddha, Jewel Flower Virtue Buddha, Seeing All Meanings Buddha,
and Tathāgata Like Mount Sumeru Buddha— these and others, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
With single-minded devotion, one should prostrate to the hundred trillion Buddhas of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss offered at dawn,

as well as to all the Buddhas of the ten directions and three periods of time offered at all times. (One should visualize all sentient beings of the West, vertically exhaustive and horizontally pervasive...)
Performing the Buddha-work, I rejoice in and equally cultivate offerings for all such successive and inexhaustible merits. Next, holding incense, one says:
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate before Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, whose lifespan is immeasurable and boundless for incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas.

(Mentally conceive of this as both the immediate retribution and the ultimate Dharma: the nature of my own mind and that of all sentient beings is luminous yet eternally quiescent; fundamentally, it is identical in essence with that of Amitābha.)
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss,

whose immeasurable light illuminates the lands of the ten directions (contemplating that this very act is both the Dharma-body and the Reward-body, universally uprooting the sufferings of the nine realms for all sentient beings and enabling them to attain the bliss of the Buddha-realm, being equally bathed by his light). With single-minded devotion,
I prostrate to Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, who appears before one at the moment of death to guide and lead the way.

[Visualize Amitābha Buddha as both the Truth and the Response. Pray that at all times, up until the moment of death, you may clearly behold him and personally hear his Dharma voice; you should respond by shedding tears with redoubled sorrow and urgency. Furthermore, holding incense, he says:

"With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* spoken by the Buddha. [This is a teaching difficult for all the worlds to believe; now that I have been able to believe and accept it, I should regard it with the utmost reverence. [Thus one should contemplate.]”
"The Dharma-nature of true emptiness is like space; The eternally abiding Dharma-treasure is inconceivable.
I manifest before all these Dharma-treasures; With a single mind, according to the Dharma, I take refuge and pay homage.
(The following two prostrations are the same).
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate and praise the *Sūtra on the Merit of Inconceivable Adoration and the Protection and Mindfulness of All Buddhas*.

With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to that which was spoken by Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, as well as to all the honored sūtras of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
(Visualize the Guiding Teacher, the Original Teacher, and the Dharma-treasures of all Buddhas brilliantly manifest within the site of enlightenment.)

With single-minded devotion, prostrate to the infinite, truly pure, radiant, and manifold jewel-colored objects of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss (one should pre-visualize these so that they appear instantaneously at the time of prostration and visualization.

The following five sensory objects are all transformations produced by Amitābha Buddha from his own pure mind; each and every one is the entire reality-nature (*dharmatā*) of the Teacher. Contemplate thus:
"The Dharma-body of the Tathāgata is like space; The manifested activities abiding in the world are inconceivable."
Before I manifest all these transformations, With single-minded devotion, I take refuge and pay homage according to the Dharma.
(The following four prostrations and the verse are the same as above.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the harmonious, elegant, subtle, and immeasurably pure sense-object of sound in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.

[Visualize that the birds of the heavens of form, the rows of trees, and the nets all produce immeasurable wondrous sounds, as do all the Dharma-sounds of the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and others; these all manifest within the site of enlightenment.
With single-minded devotion, prostrate to the infinite clouds of bodies, rains of flowers, and truly pure fragrant dust of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*).
[Visualize that all the various fragrances of the environment and the beings themselves manifest within the site of enlightenment.]

With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the infinite, truly pure objects of taste—the food and dhyāna-methods of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss (imagine that the present site of practice is now in the West;
whether eating, walking, sitting, recollecting the Buddha, the Dharma, or the Sangha, at all times there is no difference).
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the infinite, truly pure objects of touch—the virtuous waters and gentle breezes of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.

Imagine that the present site of enlightenment is no different from when [the Buddhas] were bathing, walking, offering flowers, eating, dressing, or practicing meditation in the Western Land. Next, hold up the incense and say:

With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, who extend their hands together with the Buddha in the Land of Ultimate Bliss in the West, as well as the assembly of all holy Bodhisattvas. (I pray that at all times and especially at the moment of death, I may clearly behold you.)
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to all the noble and virtuous ones of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss,

the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who are in their final birth before attaining perfect enlightenment (visualizing these immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable Great Beings of Equal Enlightenment simultaneously offering words of comfort and extending their hands).
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the immeasurable and boundless great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.

With single-minded devotion, he prostrated at the feet of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who have attained non-retrogression (*avaivartika*) in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*), whose lifespans are equal to those of the Buddha, and who have been reborn there from the ten directions.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the immeasurable and boundless śrāvaka disciples and great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss (who,
though having realized the minor fruits, are in reality similar in rank to bodhisattvas).
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas within the railings and rows of trees of the World of Ultimate Bliss (visualize them as...).

The balustrades, walking paths, and rows of trees appear vividly within the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*). I, together with them, prostrate and receive the Dharma therein. (All that follows is identical in intent.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to all the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas within the jeweled ponds and lotuses of the World of Ultimate Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*).
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to all the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas upon the stairways, pathways, and pavilions of the World of Ultimate Bliss.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to all the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who delight in celestial flowers and music upon the golden ground of the Land of Ultimate Bliss;

with single-minded devotion, I pay homage to all the Bodhisattvas who cause a profusion of exquisite flowers to flourish throughout the Land of Ultimate Bliss as they extensively perform the Buddha-work.
With single-minded devotion, they prostrate to the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the world of Ultimate Bliss who eat and practice walking meditation;
with single-minded devotion, they prostrate to the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the world of Ultimate Bliss who maintain right mindfulness upon hearing sounds.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to all the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, where there is no suffering and only various joys are experienced.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to Mañjuśrī the Dharma Prince, the Bodhisattva Ajita, and Gandhahasti.

The Bodhisattvas—such as the Bodhisattva Constantly Diligent (常精進) and all other great Bodhisattvas, as well as all Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas of the ten directions and the three periods of time (all these Bodhisattvas together receive the Buddha’s words, are born together in the Western Land, and together extend their hands to guide others;
hereafter the same)—with one mind prostrate themselves before the Venerable Śāriputra, the Venerable Kāśyapa, and the Venerable Ānanda. Thus [they did].
[Visualize] all the great disciples and all the holy Sangha of the ten directions and the three periods of time. (Having completed the visualization verse, visualize again:

"I and all sentient beings, from beginningless time, have been constantly obstructed by the heavy sins of the three karmas and six sense faculties. We have not seen the Buddhas nor known the essential way of escape.
We have merely followed the cycle of birth and death and failed to understand the wondrous principle. Although I now know it, I still [share this with all...]"

Sentient beings are alike; they are all obstructed by grave transgressions. Now, before Amitābha and the Buddhas of the ten directions, I universally take refuge and repent on behalf of all sentient beings.
I only pray that you will grant your protection so that these obstructions may be extinguished. (Having visualized this, kneel and say:)
For the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm, I vow to sever the three obstacles and take refuge through repentance. (Recite while bowing with visualization:

"From beginningless time until now, both I and all sentient beings, due to craving and false views, have internally clung to the notions of self and person, and externally associated with evil friends.
We have failed to rejoice in even a hair’s breadth of another’s goodness, but instead, throughout our three karmic activities, we have extensively committed grave offenses."
Although the actual deeds were not extensive, the evil mind was pervasive; day and night it continued without interruption.
One concealed and denied one's faults, having no desire for others to know them; one feared not the miserable realms, lacking both shame and remorse, and repudiating cause and effect.
Therefore, on this day, one now deeply believes in cause and effect, gives rise to profound shame and remorse, and feels great dread.

Reveal and repent; sever the mind of continuity. Generate the bodhicitta to abandon evil and cultivate good, diligently exerting the three karmas to overturn past grave transgressions. Rejoice in even a hair’s breadth of merit belonging to ordinary beings and sages alike.

Contemplate that the Buddhas of the ten directions possess great merit and wisdom, capable of rescuing and delivering myself and all sentient beings from the sea of the two deaths and placing us in the [Threefold]...
O Virtuous Shore! Since beginningless time, I have been ignorant of the fact that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty and quiescent; thus, I have extensively committed various evils.
Now, knowing this emptiness and quiescence, I seek Bodhi and, for the sake of sentient beings, extensively cultivate all manner of goodness and universally sever all evils.
I only pray that the Buddhas of the ten directions and the World-Honored One Amitābha will compassionately receive me and grant me leave to repent. Having visualized this:
Still kneeling on the ground, he prostrated again and said:
"With a sincere heart, I repent. I, the disciple [Name], and all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm, from time immemorial have been shrouded by ignorance and deluded by inverted views.
Consequently, through the six sense organs and the three karmas, we have practiced unwholesome dharmas and extensively committed the ten [non-virtues]."

Evil deeds and all five crimes of immediate retribution—these and all other offenses are immeasurable and boundless, such that they cannot be fully described. The Buddhas of the ten directions eternally abide in the world;
their primary and secondary adornments and the sounds of the Dharma never cease. Sublime fragrances fill all space and the flavor of the Dharma overflows the void.
They radiate pure light that illuminates and touches all beings. The eternally abiding wondrous principle pervades the entirety of empty space. From my beginningless...
Within the six sense organs, the three karmas are blind and shrouded in darkness; one neither sees, nor hears, nor perceives, nor knows.
Due to these causes and conditions, one flows long through birth and death, traversing the evil realms for hundreds of thousands of myriads of kalpas without any prospect of escape.
As the Sūtra says: "Vairocana pervades all places; the dwelling place of that Buddha is called the Light of Eternal Quiescence. Therefore, one should know this one [truth].
All phenomena are none other than the Buddha-dharma; yet I did not understand this and followed the flow of ignorance.
Thus, within Bodhi I perceived impurity, and within liberation I gave rise to fetters. Now I have finally awakened; now I have finally repented.
Facing all Buddhas and the World-Honored One Amitābha, I confess and repent my transgressions. May it cause me and the Dharma-realm...
Sentient beings, regarding the three karmas and six sense organs created since beginningless time—whether performed in the present, the past, or the future;

whether committed by oneself, incited in others, or rejoiced in upon seeing or hearing; whether remembered or forgotten, recognized or unrecognized, doubted or not doubted, concealed or revealed—all such grave offenses are ultimately purified.
Having repented, my six sense organs and three karmas are pure and free from blemish. What I have cultivated...

May all my roots of goodness likewise be purified. May they all be dedicated toward adorning the Pure Land, so that I may be born together with all sentient beings in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (An-yang).
[○@叩] I pray that Amitābha Buddha will constantly come to protect and sustain me, causing my roots of goodness to manifest and increase before me, so that I do not lose the pure cause.
At the time of passing away, may my body and mind be possessed of right mindfulness, and may my sight and hearing be clear and distinct. [○@叩] May I personally behold Amitābha...
Buddha Tathāgata, together with the assembly of holy ones, holds a flower pedestal in his hand to welcome me. In a single kṣaṇa, I am born before the Buddha.

Possessing the path of a bodhisattva, I shall extensively deliver sentient beings so that we may together achieve the wisdom of all modes (sarvākārajñatā). (Recite this three times. Then rise and chant in response:)
Having finished the repentance and made the vows, take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha and all the Triple Gem.

(Visualize the Teacher seated in the center acting as the master of your repentance, with the entire Triple Gem serving as witnesses. Having visualized the verse, next stand up and hold the incense burner. Visualize the Triple Gem above filling the ritual arena;
your own body, speech, and mind are like echoes, shadows, and flames—whether one or many, they are without confusion or obstruction. Circumambulate the Dharma seat calmly and steadily, reciting:)
Homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions (those who all extol the Pure Land).

Homage to the Dharma of the ten directions (the Dharma that is difficult for all worlds to believe, which is the ocean of the Dharma-realm; there is no Dharma-gate of the ten directions that does not flow from this Dharma-realm, and none that does not return to this Dharma-realm).
Homage to the Sangha of the ten directions (all the jewels of the Sangha throughout the ten directions of this world and the West who all incline toward the Pure Land).
Homage to the Original Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha. Homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Homage to the *Sūtra on the Protection and Mindfulness by All Buddhas*. Homage to Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.

Homage to Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta. (Recite three times. After finishing the recitation of the *Amitābha Sūtra*, recite again three times. While reciting, enter into contemplation according to the text, clearly and distinctly.)

It is clearly manifest. Yet names, phrases, and syllables are like the tracks of birds in the sky—unfathomable. Thus, they are able to perform the Buddha-work throughout the worlds of the ten directions. Next, as you arrange the incense burner, recite: "I take refuge in the Buddha;
may all sentient beings realize and understand the Great Way and give rise to the unsurpassed mind. I take refuge in the Dharma;
may all sentient beings enter deeply into the treasury of the scriptures, their wisdom becoming like the ocean."
Taking refuge in the Sangha, I vow that all sentient beings shall govern the great assembly without any hindrance;

I pay homage to the noble multitude. (Next, go to a separate place and sit upright facing west according to the Dharma. Hold the Name with single-mindedness and without distraction. A brief summary of the path of contemplation follows below. The Sutra says:
"One cannot be born in that land by means of few roots of goodness, merit, or causal conditions. (The correct path to Bodhi is called "good.")

The roots are the direct causes. Various aids to the path, such as giving, ethical discipline, and meditation, are called merit; these are the auxiliary conditions. To simply hold the name with faith and aspiration means that each and every utterance of the name is endowed with many virtuous causes and meritorious conditions.

one believes that Amitābha Buddha exists in the West, yet has not yet realized that "this mind creates the Buddha" and "this mind is the Buddha. One merely possesses resolute...

Preface to the *Ten Doubts Regarding the Pure Land* by Yang Jie, the "Man from Wúwéi" of the Song Dynasty: "If love is not deep, one will not be born in Saṃbhava; if mindfulness is not single-minded, one will not be born in Sukhāvatī.

It is immeasurable. This Sahā world is replete with all manner of suffering, whereas that land is free from suffering. In this Sahā world, beings revolve through birth and death according to their karma;

Yet it is not so; how lamentable this is! Amitābha Buddha is the Lord who embraces the Pure Land;

It is because of genuine shame and fear. Although one may possess many good deeds, if one lacks a sincere mind, a profound mind, a mind of dedication, and a mind of aspiration, then one will not attain birth in the highest of the high grades.
Alas! Amitābha is very easy to hold fast to; the Pure Land is very easy to go to.
